// Aliased so lint rules don't mistake the registration call for a React hook.
import { init as initChart, use as register } from "echarts/core"
import {
  BarChart,
  BoxplotChart,
  CandlestickChart,
  CustomChart,
  FunnelChart,
  GaugeChart,
  GraphChart,
  HeatmapChart,
  LineChart,
  ParallelChart,
  PictorialBarChart,
  PieChart,
  RadarChart,
  SankeyChart,
  ScatterChart,
  SunburstChart,
  ThemeRiverChart,
  TreeChart,
  TreemapChart,
} from "echarts/charts"
import {
  CalendarComponent,
  GraphicComponent,
  GridComponent,
  LegendComponent,
  MarkAreaComponent,
  MarkLineComponent,
  MarkPointComponent,
  ParallelComponent,
  PolarComponent,
  RadarComponent,
  SingleAxisComponent,
  TooltipComponent,
  VisualMapContinuousComponent,
} from "echarts/components"
// ECharts 6 ignores `grid.containLabel` unless LegacyGridContainLabel is registered.
import { LabelLayout, LegacyGridContainLabel } from "echarts/features"
import { CanvasRenderer } from "echarts/renderers"

let registered = false

/**
 * Registers only what these charts draw, on first use. Calling it from `init` keeps it reachable,
 * so bundlers honouring the package's `sideEffects` list never drop it from production builds.
 */
const ensureRegistered = () => {
  if (registered) return
  registered = true
  register([
    BarChart,
    BoxplotChart,
    CandlestickChart,
    CustomChart,
    FunnelChart,
    GaugeChart,
    GraphChart,
    HeatmapChart,
    LineChart,
    ParallelChart,
    PictorialBarChart,
    PieChart,
    RadarChart,
    SankeyChart,
    ScatterChart,
    SunburstChart,
    ThemeRiverChart,
    TreeChart,
    TreemapChart,
    CalendarComponent,
    GraphicComponent,
    GridComponent,
    LegendComponent,
    MarkAreaComponent,
    MarkLineComponent,
    MarkPointComponent,
    ParallelComponent,
    PolarComponent,
    RadarComponent,
    SingleAxisComponent,
    TooltipComponent,
    VisualMapContinuousComponent,
    LabelLayout,
    LegacyGridContainLabel,
    CanvasRenderer,
  ])
}

export const init: typeof initChart = (...args) => {
  ensureRegistered()
  return initChart(...args)
}
export type { EChartsType } from "echarts/core"
export type { EChartsOption } from "echarts"

import type { ReactNode } from "react"
import { cx } from "../../../utils/cx.js"

/** Edge fades shared by every pattern-style background. */
export type BackdropMask = "none" | "radial" | "top" | "bottom" | "edges"

export const hasChildren = (children: ReactNode): boolean =>
  children !== undefined &&
  children !== null &&
  children !== false &&
  children !== true &&
  children !== ""

/**
 * Every background renders the same shell: on its own it is a full-bleed, inert, aria-hidden
 * layer (`position: absolute; inset: 0`); given children it becomes an isolated wrapper that
 * paints the effect behind them, so content never needs its own z-index.
 */
export const backdropRoot = (
  base: string,
  className: string | undefined,
  wrapper: boolean,
) => ({
  className: cx(base, className),
  "data-wrapper": wrapper || undefined,
  "aria-hidden": wrapper ? undefined : (true as const),
})

/** `useId` output contains characters that are awkward inside `url(#…)` references. */
export const svgId = (prefix: string, reactId: string): string =>
  `${prefix}-${reactId.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, "")}`

interface DotPatternSvgProps {
  id: string
  gap: number
  radius: number
  className: string
}

/** One dot per cell, centred so the pattern tiles symmetrically from any edge. */
export const DotPatternSvg = ({ id, gap, radius, className }: DotPatternSvgProps) => (
  <svg className={className} width="100%" height="100%" aria-hidden="true">
    <defs>
      <pattern id={id} width={gap} height={gap} patternUnits="userSpaceOnUse">
        <circle cx={gap / 2} cy={gap / 2} r={radius} fill="currentColor" />
      </pattern>
    </defs>
    <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill={`url(#${id})`} />
  </svg>
)

/** Lays digits into the pattern, dropping trailing literals so deleting stays natural. */
export const formatPhone = (digits: string, pattern: string): string => {
  let out = ""
  let index = 0
  for (const char of pattern) {
    if (index >= digits.length) break
    if (char === "#") out += digits[index++]
    else out += char
  }
  return out + digits.slice(index)
}

export const maxDigits = (pattern: string): number => pattern.split("#").length - 1

/** Elements a text effect can render as through its `as` prop. */
export type TextEffectElement =
  | "h1"
  | "h2"
  | "h3"
  | "h4"
  | "h5"
  | "h6"
  | "p"
  | "span"
  | "div"
  | "strong"
  | "em"
  | "blockquote"
  | "figcaption"
  | "label"

export interface TextToken {
  type: "word" | "space"
  value: string
  /** Grapheme clusters, so emoji, flags and combining marks are never torn apart. */
  chars: string[]
}

let segmenter: Intl.Segmenter | null | undefined

export const graphemes = (value: string): string[] => {
  if (segmenter === undefined) {
    segmenter =
      typeof Intl !== "undefined" && "Segmenter" in Intl
        ? new Intl.Segmenter(undefined, { granularity: "grapheme" })
        : null
  }
  return segmenter
    ? Array.from(segmenter.segment(value), (part) => part.segment)
    : Array.from(value)
}

// Whitespace runs stay verbatim text nodes so the browser collapses and wraps them as usual.
// No-break spaces are not separators: they belong to the word they glue together.
const SEPARATOR = /([^\S\u00a0]+)/

export const tokenize = (text: string): TextToken[] =>
  text
    .split(SEPARATOR)
    .filter((value) => value !== "")
    .map((value): TextToken =>
      SEPARATOR.test(value) && value.trim() === ""
        ? { type: "space", value, chars: [] }
        : { type: "word", value, chars: graphemes(value) },
    )
